topic_name: The Concept, Essence and Functions of Culture

1.question: The original meaning of the Latin cultura that explains the shift from the tilling of land to the cultivation of the human being is...

options.A: Cultivation and improvement
options.C: Imitation and depiction
options.D: Arrangement and ordering
options.E: Dwelling and settling of space

2.question: The transfer of the notion of cultivation to the "culture of the soul" is associated with the name of...

options.A: Quintilian
options.C: Seneca
options.D: Cicero
options.E: Lucretius

3.question: The ancient Greek concept of "paideia" is closest to culture primarily in the sense of...

options.A: Education and learnedness
options.C: Economic calculation
options.D: Ritual purification
options.E: Civil legislation

4.question: The statement that conveys J.-J. Rousseau's assessment of culture:

options.A: The development of culture is derived from the stylistic unity of an era
options.B: The development of culture necessarily improves morals
options.C: The development of culture is an alternation of closed organisms
options.D: The development of culture may destroy natural human bonds
options.E: The development of culture is determined by the amount of energy harnessed

5.question: The thinker with whom the use of "culture" as an independent concept is associated is...

options.A: W. von Humboldt
options.C: S. Pufendorf
options.D: J. G. Herder
options.E: W. Ostwald

6.question: The correct pairing of a thinker and his position on culture and civilization:

options.A: Tylor draws a boundary between them; Humboldt equates the concepts
options.B: Spengler draws a boundary between them; Kant equates the concepts
options.C: Herder draws a boundary between them; Tylor opposes the concepts
options.D: Kant draws a boundary between them; Spengler opposes the concepts
options.E: Fichte draws a boundary between them; Pufendorf opposes the concepts

7.question: The image of culture as a critical mirror in which a person recognizes himself belongs to...

options.A: G. Marcel
options.C: A. Camus
options.D: M. Heidegger
options.E: K. Jaspers

8.question: The interpretation of culture as "the veneration of light" is presented as an interpretation by...

options.A: V. Solovyov
options.C: N. Berdyaev
options.D: S. Bulgakov
options.E: N. Roerich

9.question: What makes it possible to reconcile the natural prerequisites of culture with its supernatural character?

options.A: Social organization reproduces the structure of a biological organism
options.B: The division of labour in itself abolishes human dependence on nature
options.C: A natural creator goes beyond instinct in his activity
options.D: Cultural norms represent inherited forms of species behaviour
options.E: The transformation of the environment changes tools while preserving natural motivation

10.question: Why can the ashes and broken branches left behind by an expedition be regarded as cultural phenomena?

options.A: They possess shared symbolism fixed by the expedition's ritual
options.B: They record human intervention in the natural environment
options.C: They are a documentary message with an established code
options.D: They constitute a deliberately created artistic statement
options.E: They embody value models specially selected by society

11.question: How are education, upbringing and culture related?

options.A: Education replaces cultural continuity with individual experience
options.B: Mastery of culture precedes any interaction with society
options.C: Education produces culture, while upbringing reproduces biological properties
options.D: Upbringing transmits culture, while education operates outside it
options.E: Education and upbringing ensure the mastery of previously created culture

12.question: The main function of culture, from which all the others are derived, is called the...

options.A: Regulative function
options.C: Axiological function
options.D: Semiotic function
options.E: Humanistic (human-shaping) function

13.question: Which name is identified with the function of historical continuity?

options.A: Evaluative
options.C: Normative
options.D: Cognitive
options.E: Semiotic

14.question: Cultural memory differs from a passive store of information...

options.A: By the complete reproduction of the original form of any custom
options.B: By the predominant recording of events in official documents
options.C: By the obligatory replacement of oral inheritance with written archives
options.D: By the selection and active transmission of significant models
options.E: By the preservation of all information with equal social priority

15.question: The accumulation of the experience of many generations creates the conditions for knowing the world. Which function of culture is revealed in this statement?

options.A: Regulative
options.C: Cognitive
options.D: Humanistic (human-shaping)
options.E: Informational

16.question: Name the normative systems on which the regulative function of culture primarily relies.

options.A: The scientific paradigm
options.C: The mythological plot
options.D: Morality
options.E: Law

17.question: The condition for mastering art and science that the semiotic function of culture emphasizes is...

options.A: Accumulation of knowledge about the historical environment of a work
options.C: Reconciling personal experience with the social ideal
options.D: Acceptance of a shared hierarchy of artistic values
options.E: Recognition of the normative authority of a cultural institution

18.question: The formation of a person's value needs and orientations expresses the ... function.

options.A: Cognitive
options.C: Semiotic
options.D: Informational
options.E: Communicative

19.question: The object of assessment that corresponds to the evaluative function is...

options.A: The conformity of personal preferences to a hierarchy of recognized values
options.B: The reliability of a report on events of the cultural past
options.C: The influence of cultural forms on a person's social and spiritual qualities
options.D: The consistency of a person's behaviour with prevailing norms
options.E: The effectiveness of the transmission of social experience between generations

20.question: The general regularities of cultural development include...

options.A: The dependence of a cultural event on preceding events
options.B: The possible mismatch between the rhythms of economic and cultural life
options.C: A single sequence of strategic factors among all peoples
options.D: The same speed of transformation of material and spiritual forms
options.E: A direct correspondence between technical growth and moral improvement

21.question: The "strategic variable" in the development of culture means...

options.A: A sum of random changes devoid of cultural consequences
options.B: An individual preference unconnected with the life of society
options.C: A factor that acquires special significance under given historical conditions
options.D: A single cause acting equally among all peoples
options.E: An unchanging set of values of all cultural-historical types

22.question: The most stable side of culture includes:

options.A: Artistic manifestos of new schools
options.C: Rites and customs
options.D: Habitual values and norms
options.E: Experimental technical methods

23.question: Which pairing of a cultural bearer and a line of development is incorrect?

options.A: Scientific creativity: the innovative line of culture
options.B: The peasantry: preservation of stable traditional models
options.C: The popular mentality: resistance to external influences
options.D: The peasantry: the leading bearer of scientific and technological innovation
options.E: The city: a centre of scientific and technological innovation

24.question: The ideal of the human being that corresponds to the Renaissance is...

options.A: A fully developed personality with freedom to choose a path in life
options.B: A performer of an inherited function within an unchanging order
options.C: A person who has achieved success through personal merit
options.D: A religious ascetic who rejects sensual pleasures
options.E: A citizen of physical perfection and joyful knowledge of the world

25.question: Indicate the correct pairings of a cultural-studies discipline and its task.

options.A: History of culture: description of concrete historical development
options.B: Theory of culture: exclusively the dating of archaeological finds
options.C: Philosophy of culture: exclusively statistics of cultural consumption
options.D: History of culture: establishing universal biological laws
options.E: Philosophy of culture: choosing general cognitive orientations
